exposure: Maternal population group (Turkish citizen vs. Syrian refugee)
cohort: The study included 4,170 adolescent mothers (aged 15-19) delivering at a tertiary hospital in Turkiye, comprising both Turkish citizens and Syrian refugees.
finding: Syrian refugee adolescent mothers had significantly higher rates of general anesthesia and cesarean sections compared to Turkish citizen adolescent mothers, and neonates born under spinal anesthesia showed higher APGAR scores.
mod_finding: Syrian refugee adolescent mothers had a higher cesarean section rate (48.8%) compared to Turkish citizen adolescent mothers (45.4%).
